content.title: About
content.content: Marshmallows are soft confections made from sugar, syrup, gelatin, and whipped egg whites. They have a light, fluffy texture and a sweet taste, often coated in chocolate or dusted with powdered sugar. Marshmallows are popular as a snack, a baking ingredient, and a festive treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally marshmallows were made from the sap of the marshmallow plant (Althaea officinalis).
Modern marshmallows use gelatin, but vegan versions exist using agar‑agar or pectin.
Marshmallows are a key component of the classic American dessert “s’mores” with chocolate and graham crackers.
In Japan, “fluffy” marshmallows are shaped into cute figures and flavored with a variety of tastes.
During space missions, marshmallows were used as a lightweight snack because they don’t crumble and store well.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The sugar in marshmallows is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate glucose boost.

items.title: Lightweight snack
items.content: Low density makes them convenient for on‑the‑go consumption during active events.

items.title: Contains gelatin
items.content: Gelatin is rich in collagen, which supports skin, hair, and joint health.

items.title: Soothes the throat
items.content: Their soft texture and sweetness can ease discomfort from colds or irritated throats.

items.title: Flavor versatility
items.content: Marshmallows can be easily flavored, allowing the addition of vitamins and plant extracts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the gelatin used in traditional marshmallows.

items.title: Not suitable for vegans
items.content: Traditional products contain animal gelatin, so vegans should choose alternative versions.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Soft yet sticky pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marshmallows can be enjoyed on their own, added to hot chocolate, used in baking, as cake decorations, or in s’mores. They can also be toasted over a flame for a caramelized exterior.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store marshmallows in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent melting and texture loss. Keep them away from moisture, which can make them sticky.

content.title: About
content.content: Eel is a marine fish of the family Anguillidae, found in rivers, lakes and coastal seas of the Northern Hemisphere. Its flesh is dark‑red, firm, and has a slightly sweet flavor. Eel is commonly used in sushi, grilling, smoking, and traditional dishes such as Japanese “unagi.”

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eels can migrate between fresh and salt water, undertaking a spawning migration known as the “silver eel” phase.
In Japan, eel is a delicacy often served as grilled “unagi” with a sweet soy‑based sauce.
There are over 800 eel species, but the European (Anguilla anguilla) and American (Anguilla rostrata) eels are most commonly used in cuisine.
Eels produce a mucus layer that protects their skin from parasites and infections.
In some cultures, eel symbolizes longevity and strength.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Eel meat contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Eel provides a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eel is a good source of B12, B1 and B6, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals aid hemoglobin formation and immune support.

items.title: Vitamin A
items.content: Supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked eel may contain parasites; it should be cooked to at least 70 °C.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Marinated or smoked eel can be high in salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may react to eel.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: Eels from polluted waters can accumulate cadmium and mercury; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eel can be grilled, baked, steamed, or smoked. In Japan it is often served as “unagi” grilled with a sweet soy glaze. The flesh is sliced thin for sushi, added to salads, or used in stews. Before cooking, remove the skin and innards.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh eel should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it at –18 °C in an airtight bag. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Non‑dairy frozen dessert (2218) is a frozen treat made from plant‑based ingredients such as coconut milk, almond milk, or soy cream. It contains no dairy, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance, while offering a creamy texture and a wide range of flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first vegan ice cream appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Emulsifiers like guar gum or carrageenan are often used to achieve a “milky” mouthfeel.
Natural flavorings (berries, fruits, spices) allow for more than 30 distinct taste profiles.
Some brands use fermented nut pastes, giving the dessert a subtle tang.
Non‑dairy ice cream typically has lower saturated fat but can be rich in healthy fats from nuts and coconut.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Plant bases often contain probiotics and prebiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: The absence of milk sugar makes the product safe for those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Coconut milk and nut pastes provide medium‑chain triglycerides and monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Depending on the base, the dessert can supply vitamin E, magnesium, calcium, and iron.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Natural flavorings such as berries or cocoa contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Nut and soy allergies
items.content: Many plant bases are derived from nuts or soy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: To enhance taste, added sugars or syrups are common; people monitoring blood glucose should choose unsweetened versions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even without dairy fats, the dessert can be calorie‑dense due to plant oils.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Emulsifiers and stabilizers (carrageenan, guar gum) are generally safe, but some consumers prefer minimally processed products.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve non‑dairy frozen dessert like any ice cream: in cones, cups, as ice‑cream sandwiches, or blended into smoothies. Pair with berries, nuts, toasted coconut, or a dark‑chocolate sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to prevent ice crystal formation. Avoid thawing and refreezing to maintain texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Taco is a popular Mexican dish consisting of a soft or crunchy corn (sometimes wheat) shell filled with meat, vegetables, cheese, and sauces. The NFS (New Flavor Series) version offers a unique blend of spices and aromas designed for a bolder taste experience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic taco originated in Mexico in the early 19th century as street food.
The word “taco” comes from Mexican Spanish, meaning “wrapper” or “plug”.
In the United States more than 3 billion tacos are consumed each year, making it one of the most popular fast‑food items.
The NFS variant uses a mix of smoked chipotle, lime zest, and aromatic herbs not found in traditional recipes.
Traditional Mexican tacos are often served with salsa, guacamole, and lime wedges.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Fillings such as beef, chicken, or beans provide quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain shells contain thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain corn shells add dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When prepared by grilling or baking rather than deep‑frying, tacos contain minimal trans fats, which is better for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Chipotle, paprika, and lime are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and ready‑made seasoning mixes can be salty, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fatty fillings
items.content: Fatty cuts of meat or large amounts of cheese increase calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to corn shells.

items.title: Spicy foods
items.content: Hot sauces can irritate the stomach and esophagus in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tacos can be enjoyed warm or hot, filling the shell with meat, beans, fresh vegetables, cheese, and your favorite sauces. For a lighter option, choose whole‑grain shells and lean chicken or turkey fillings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry corn shells in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 2 weeks. Cooked fillings should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Water NFS is a pure drinking water obtained through reverse osmosis and enhanced mineralization. The product contains no calories, sugar, or artificial additives, providing optimal hydration for the body.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Water NFS undergoes triple filtration: carbon filter, membrane osmosis, and UV treatment.
Mineralization adds calcium, magnesium and potassium in natural ratios.
The PET bottle is fully recyclable and meets international food‑grade safety standards.
Produced according to GOST 31971‑2012, guaranteeing the absence of microbiological contaminants.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Regular consumption of pure water helps maintain fluid balance, essential for all physiological processes.

items.title: Reduces kidney load
items.content: Lack of sugar and artificial additives lowers the risk of kidney stone formation.

items.title: Maintains electrolyte balance
items.content: Minerals such as calcium and magnesium support normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Aids weight control
items.content: Water contains no calories, so replacing sugary drinks with it can help lower overall dietary calorie intake.

items.title: Improves skin condition
items.content: Adequate water intake helps keep skin hydrated and assists in toxin elimination.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Drinking excessive amounts of water can lead to hyponatremia – dilution of blood sodium levels.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some individuals may react to the added minerals, although such cases are rare.

items.title: Plastic containers
items.content: When stored for long periods in hot conditions, plastic may release microscopic particles; store in a cool place.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Water NFS is best consumed plain, chilled or at room temperature. It works well as a base for herbal teas, smoothies, and sports drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, it is recommended to consume within 3‑5 days.
